title: My Letters!
text:
My letters! Dead paper... mute and white...

And nevertheless tonight they beat

in my trembling hands when I loosen

the ribbon and they fall upon my knees.


This one said: Give me your friendship...

This one fixed a day in spring

to touch my hand... almost nothing,

but how I wept! This one... a paper...


said: I love you, and I shuddered

as if God had torn my past.

This one: I am yours... the ink pale


from being beside a tumultuous breast.

And this last one... oh, love!, I would not be worthy

of what you say if I repeated it.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the letters as dead paper that still physically pulses in the speaker's hands.

title: The World Seems So Different to Me
text:
The world seems so different to me

since I heard the steps of your soul,

very light, yes, very light, beside me,

on the terrible shore of death

where I was going to drown, and love

saved me by revealing to me a life

made of new music. Those bitters

appointed by God I want to drink,

singing their sweetness, beside you.

Place names are different

because you are or will be here or there.

And that gift of singing I loved so much

(the angels know it) is dear to me

only because it makes your name resound.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's transformation of the whole world through the beloved's soul-steps.

title: Oh, My Love, My Love
text:
Oh, my love, my love, when I think

that you already existed then, a year ago,

when I was alone here in the snow

and did not see your footprints or hear

your voice in the silence... My chain,

link by link, I was measuring

as if I could not see myself freed

by your possible hand... Until I drank

the prodigious cup of life!

How strange not to feel you in the trembling

of day or night, voice, presence,

nor to divine you in those white flowers!

I was blind just like the atheist

who does not discover the God he cannot see.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the retrospective astonishment that the beloved existed before being recognized.

title: How Do I Love You?
text:
How do I love you? Well, I love you

to the abyss and to the highest region

I can reach when I pursue

the limits of Being and the Ideal.


I love you in the most everyday living,

with the sun and by candlelight.

With freedom, as one aspires to Good;

with the innocence of one who longs for glory.


I love you with the fever I once put

into my grief and with my childhood faith,

with the love I thought I lost


when I lost my saints... With the tears

and smiles of my life... And if God wills,

I will love you much more after death.
editorial_note: The translation follows the Spanish version of Browning's famous sonnet rather than quoting the canonical English.
